extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism finalization from paper-local XML, tables, figure captions, and PDF text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LabyA1 is supported as an HIV/HSV entry-stage inhibitor by time-of-drug-addition assays.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=4:Figure 4;xml:sec=Results:LabyA1 interferes with the viral replication at an early time point

mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay localizes inhibition to early entry timing; it does not by itself define a single molecular binding site.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SPR data support direct interaction of LabyA1 with immobilized HIV-1 gp120 proteins with micromolar KD values.

source_locator.locator: xml:table=5:rows=3-5;xml:sec=Results:Interaction of LabyA1 with the Envelope Protein gp120 of HIV

mechanism_claims.limitations: Binding is shown to gp120 proteins, while exact epitope/glycan specificity is not resolved here.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Flow-cytometry and calcium-mobilization experiments do not support CD4, CXCR4, or CCR5 receptor blockade as the main LabyA1 mechanism.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=5:Figure 5;xml:sec=Results:No interaction of LabyA1 with the cellular receptors involved in HIV pathogenesis

mechanism_claims.limitations: Negative receptor-interaction evidence constrains mechanism but does not exclude other host or viral interactions.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Cell-cell and DC-SIGN-mediated transmission assays support antiviral activity in transmission models relevant to entry-stage spread.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Transmission inhibition is activity-context evidence and is not promoted to a unique molecular mechanism.
